$description: Canonical Alliance Protocols registry (spec v2: 15 tools, three plain tiers). Names are exact card titles.

core.label: Learn first
core.meaning: Start here. These six cover most evenings.

situational.label: When it comes up
situational.meaning: For when the Situation Map sends you there.

build.label: Build over time
build.meaning: Habits to add once the first six feel familiar.

tiers.rule: Plain words only: no dots or glyph text. Say "the six to learn first".

protocols.name: Green Rule
canonical: Comes before every other tool in the system.
Afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no? → Stop. These tools are not for this. Get outside help (see Help Lines).
A stated lack of safety is believed first.
Pause + Return is for flooding, never for fear: if threats, fear, coercion or violence appear, do not return at the set time; leave safely and use Help Lines.

protocols.name: Pause + Return
canonical: Exact return time, always.
For flooding, never for fear.
If you're the one waiting: don't follow, block the way or message during the pause. Not being allowed to leave a room or the house is a Help Lines moment, not a pause.
canonicalPhrases: at least 20 minutes and at most 24 hours away

protocols.name: 60-Second Reset
canonical: Five steps: Stop · Say one sentence · Touch (only if it's welcome) · Breathe (three slow breaths) · Return (the time you named).
The one sentence: “I want to connect, not fight. Can we talk at ___?”
Too hot to stay in the room? Pause + Return.
canonicalPhrases: I want to connect, not fight. Can we talk at ___?

protocols.name: Micro-Repair
canonical: Timing window (use everywhere, no 10-minute or 48-hour variants).
canonicalPhrases: Start within minutes if you can; finish within 24 hours

protocols.name: Weekly Reset
canonical: 5 parts, about 40 minutes (15 is fine to start): Appreciation (5 min) · Check the load (15 min) · One friction point (15 min) · Requests + Next steps (5 min).
The monthly part of your Weekly Reset adds 10 minutes; the yearly part is 1–2 hours, once a year. Never a separate meeting.
Maintenance, not a trial. Flooded? Pause + Return first.

protocols.name: System Overlay
protocols.plainEnglishSubtitle: a five-step order for hard conversations
canonical: Five steps: Warm up · Make it safe · Say what happened · Ask for one thing · Agree next steps.
Three speeds: quick (about 90 seconds), standard, and already a fight.
For “A fight is starting”, the 60-Second Reset sentence comes first; the System Overlay is the next link, not the first.
Already a fight: first check you're both calm; if either of you is flooded, take a Pause + Return.
Quick version: “Restart: same team.”
A serious hurt needs the slow version, Full Repair.

protocols.name: Full Repair
canonical: Six steps; calm, agreed, scheduled, never mid-fight or sprung on someone.
One-sided breach: only the partner who caused it acknowledges impact. Closing line only if it's true for both of you.
Either of you may say no to booking it.
Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this tool, not a failure of it.

protocols.name: Trust Recovery

numbers.window: 2–4 weeks to start (1–2 weeks for a smaller Proof item)

canonical: A breach is something the partner agrees they did. Seeing friends or family, privacy or a locked phone is never a breach. You cannot be made to accept a breach you do not agree happened.
Only the partner who broke trust acknowledges impact; the hurt partner is never asked to confess in return.
Transparency is offered voluntarily by the partner who broke trust, time-limited, and never becomes monitoring.
Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this tool, not a failure of it.

protocols.name: Check-Up
canonical: One tool, one sheet, three lenses: drifting apart, pulling away, say-and-do gaps.
Safety first: contempt, fear or coercion: stop and get outside support.
Never use the signs to question where your partner goes, who they see or what they plan. A partner who has stopped sharing because they are afraid is not pulling away: use the Help Lines.
Describe observable behaviour; don't claim to know the partner's intent. It is not a verdict.
Either of you may decline to compare counts. Agree a Full Repair date only if you both want to; either of you may say no.
Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this tool, not a failure of it.

protocols.name: Team Agreement
canonical: One step list: Believe first · Pause before reacting · Trace the source · Name the unit · Agree your response.
Whether to be out is each person's own decision. No agreement can require either of you to hide who you are or to be outed.
No tool is ever used to limit a partner's contact with friends, family, money, phone or movement.

protocols.name: Sun Memory
canonical: Pauses system-talk only, never basic communication, safety, childcare/logistics, or a scheduled repair.
Either partner may end it by naming a safety concern.

protocols.name: Daily Rhythm
canonical: Morning hello 5 minutes or less; evening catch-up about 10 minutes.
The minimum: a hello, an “I see you”, an appreciation, and a repair within 24 hours if anything stings.
Physical contact is always 'if welcome'.

protocols.name: Intimacy Pact
canonical: A “no” needs no script, reason, or substitute offer. No pact or agreement creates an obligation to sex, touch, or disclosure.
The review is about how asking and saying no feel, never about how often. Either of you can skip or postpone it. “Stalled” is never a reason to ask more.
Pressure after a no: stop; don't talk it through in the moment. The person pressured decides whether, when and with whom to talk. Force, threats, fear or a repeat: Help Lines.
Physical contact is always 'if welcome'.

protocols.name: Consistency Pact
canonical: Private weekly check; telling your partner about a broken shared agreement is part of the partnership. Your own notes, thoughts and answers are never owed.

protocols.name: Profile Calibration
canonical: Nobody has to complete this, and you can stop at any time. Do not ask your partner to show their answers.
Answers stay on your phone. The Layer Scan report shows where you differ most, layer by layer.

sun-memory.name: Sun Memory

lengths.quick: a few minutes, inside one ritual (stop the checklist, return to ease)
lengths.full: an agreed stretch of 2 to 24 hours, with no talk about the tools or what needs fixing

canonical: Pauses system-talk only, never basic communication, safety, childcare/logistics, or a scheduled repair.
Either partner may end it by naming a safety concern.
All Sun Memory safety rules apply to both lengths.
'Kill-Switch' never appears in buyer-facing text (retired in Round 10).

situation-map.name: Situation Map

rowsCanonical.label: I’m afraid, being threatened, or not free to say no
rowsCanonical.note: Includes jealousy that leads to checking, restricting or accusing. Numbers are not on the printed map: keep them somewhere private.

rowsCanonical.label: I’m flooded or shut down (but safe)
A fight is starting
rowsCanonical.route: 60-Second Reset (then Pause + Return; System Overlay is the next link)
rowsCanonical.note: One sentence first: “I want to connect, not fight. Can we talk at ___?”

rowsCanonical.label: Outside pressure or disapproval from family, friends or strangers
Trust breach
rowsCanonical.route: Trust Recovery (skip the 7-day plan; then the Weekly Reset)

rowsCanonical.label: After a fight, or something small stung
rowsCanonical.route: Micro-Repair (bigger: Full Repair; changes: a Proof item)

rowsCanonical.label: We keep clashing the same way
rowsCanonical.route: Appendix A: common patterns · Profile Calibration (+ Check-Up)

situation-map.rule: Safety row is always FIRST (step 0). Never route 'unsafe' to Pause + Return.

help-safety.name: Help Lines
helpLines: Immediate danger: your local emergency number (999 UK/SG police · 995 SG ambulance · 911 US · 000 AU · 112 EU)
US: National Domestic Violence Hotline 1-800-799-7233 (text START to 88788) · 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call/text 988)
UK: National Domestic Abuse Helpline (Refuge) 0808 2000 247 · Samaritans 116 123
Singapore: National Anti-Violence & Sexual Harassment Helpline 1800 777 0000 · SOS 1767

Sexual violence, including from a partner: US RAINN 800-656-4673 (text HOPE to 64673) · UK Rape Crisis England & Wales 0808 500 2222 · Australia 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) · Singapore AWARE Sexual Assault Care Centre 6779 0282 (weekdays 10am to 6pm)
EU: Helpline for women experiencing violence 116 016, where available
Worried about a child: your local child-protection service, or your emergency number if a child is in danger.
Elsewhere: your local emergency number or national helpline.

guardrails.safety-first-row: Afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no? → Stop. These tools are not for this. Get outside help (see Help Lines).
guardrails.leaving-is-valid: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this tool, not a failure of it.
guardrails.one-sided-breach: When one partner caused the breach, only that partner acknowledges impact; the hurt partner is never asked to confess in return. Closing/reconciliation lines are optional ('only if it's true for both of you').
guardrails.no-script-no: A “no” needs no script, reason, or substitute offer. No pact or agreement creates an obligation to sex, touch, or disclosure.
guardrails.no-limiting-contact: No tool is ever used to limit a partner's contact with friends, family, money, phone or movement.
guardrails.no-monitoring: Never 'track'/'verify' the other partner; use 'look at it together at the check-in'. Transparency is voluntary, time-limited, never monitoring.
guardrails.sexual-pressure: Pressure after a no: stop; don't talk it through in the moment. The person pressured decides whether, when and with whom to talk. Force, threats, fear or a repeat: Help Lines.
guardrails.believe-first: A stated lack of safety is believed first.
guardrails.waiting-partner: If you're the one waiting: don't follow, block the way or message during the pause. Not being allowed to leave a room or the house is a Help Lines moment, not a pause.
guardrails.breach-definition: A breach is something the partner agrees they did. Seeing friends or family, privacy or a locked phone is never a breach. You cannot be made to accept a breach you do not agree happened.
guardrails.not-a-verdict: The Check-Up describes behaviour; it is not a verdict. Never use the signs to question where your partner goes, who they see or what they plan.
guardrails.outing: Whether to be out is each person's own decision. No agreement can require either of you to hide who you are or to be outed.
guardrails.private-notes: Telling your partner about a broken shared agreement is part of the partnership. Your own notes, thoughts and answers are never owed.
guardrails.no-pressure: Nobody has to complete Profile Calibration, and you can stop at any time. Do not ask your partner to show their answers.

firstWeek.title: Your First Week
tonight: Read the red row of the Situation Map.
Agree one pause phrase and a return time. Write them where you will both see them.
Try the 60-Second Reset once, while you’re calm.
days: Say the Green Rule lines aloud
One Daily Rhythm moment: the evening catch-up
Try the quick System Overlay on one small thing
First Weekly Reset (15 minutes is fine; 40 is the full version)
